steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the core multidisciplinary team from September through November 2026. Establish its leadership, decision rights, role coverage, interfaces with product owners and specialist Digital and IT functions, initial demand pipeline and capacity plan, with the team ready for full delivery from December 2026.

outputs.title: Core team appointments
outputs.summary: Recruit or assign the agreed engineering, product and experience design, and agile delivery capacity.

outputs.title: Leadership and decision rights
outputs.summary: Confirm who leads the team, how product and technical decisions are made and how priorities are escalated.

outputs.title: Role and capability map
outputs.summary: Define core team responsibilities and the specialist architecture, data, integration, security, accessibility, change and service-management contributions it draws on.

outputs.title: Product-owner interfaces
outputs.summary: Define how the team works with the 4.1.2 Hub product and platform owner and the 4.1.4 King’s Edge product owner.

outputs.title: Initial pipeline and capacity plan
outputs.summary: Create one prioritised view of demand, available capacity, sequencing and delivery constraints.

outputs.title: Team onboarding and working agreements
outputs.summary: Establish shared goals, collaboration norms, tools and an initial rhythm for planning and review.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with King’s Edge sponsorship
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide product leadership, institutional prioritisation and resolution of competing demand across 4.1.2 and 4.1.4.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may receive conflicting demand or lack authority to protect a coherent pipeline.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide access to product, research, design, engineering, quality, change and other specialist practice leadership beyond the core funded pod.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The small core team may become isolated or unable to maintain consistent professional standards.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide named service-management and support counterparts so delivery and live operation are planned together.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may deliver capabilities without a credible route into ongoing support.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £201,000 in constant 2026 prices for November 2026 to June 2027.
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager, including hands-on technical leadership within the engineering capacity.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The institution will not establish the in-house team required to deliver the 4.1.2 and 4.1.4 product roadmaps.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the first-year team shape and recruitment route in time for recruitment to begin in September 2026.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with King’s Edge sponsorship
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The core team will not be available in November.

enablingConditions.condition: Assign named specialist contributors with protected availability and clear decision rights.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The core team may be blocked by competing specialist queues.

enablingConditions.condition: Operate one coordinated product pipeline across 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.1.4, with shared staffing held under 4.1.3 and app and platform investment held under 4.1.2.
enablingConditions.owner: King’s Edge Portfolio Board and Digital and IT
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Capacity and investment may be fragmented or double-counted.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm whether any product research, professional-development or collaboration costs cannot be absorbed through staffing and existing institutional provision before adding a separate team-practice envelope.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before the first-year operating plan is fixed
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Practice costs may either be overlooked or duplicated within the 4.1.2 platform envelope.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish how the team turns demand into delivered and supported product change. Put in place a transparent intake and prioritisation route, discovery and user-research practices, service design and prototyping methods, engineering and quality expectations, definitions of ready and done, embedded assurance workflows, release and documentation disciplines, and regular planning, review and retrospective routines.

outputs.title: Demand intake and prioritisation
outputs.summary: Create one transparent route for new demand, triage, sequencing and capacity decisions.

outputs.title: Discovery and problem definition
outputs.summary: Establish proportionate methods for understanding needs, outcomes, constraints and evidence before committing to solutions.

outputs.title: Continuous user research and service design
outputs.summary: Build student and staff involvement into discovery, design, testing and evaluation rather than treating consultation as a separate stage.

outputs.title: Prototyping and experimentation
outputs.summary: Define how assumptions are tested quickly and how experiments are bounded, evaluated and concluded.

outputs.title: Engineering and quality practices
outputs.summary: Agree code review, testing, quality engineering, technical documentation and maintainability expectations for the team.

outputs.title: Definitions and acceptance criteria
outputs.summary: Establish definitions of ready and done and clear criteria for moving from experiment to controlled live use and supported service.

outputs.title: Embedded assurance workflow
outputs.summary: Define how the team collaborates with architecture, data, security, privacy, accessibility and service management throughout delivery.

outputs.title: Delivery cadence and learning routines
outputs.summary: Establish planning, review, release, retrospective and evidence-sharing routines that support continuous improvement.

steps.title: Prove the end-to-end product lifecycle through King’s Edge
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, use the King’s Edge roadmap to run repeated end-to-end product cycles. Move needs through discovery, design, prototyping, development, quality and assurance, controlled release and evaluation, then either harden successful changes for continued service or conclude them cleanly. Use the evidence to refine team roles, practices and handoffs.

outputs.title: Repeated end-to-end delivery cycles
outputs.summary: Demonstrate that several distinct Edge needs can move predictably from discovery into evaluated live use.

outputs.title: Continuous student and service involvement
outputs.summary: Show that users and operational owners influence decisions throughout each delivery cycle.

outputs.title: Assurance integrated into delivery
outputs.summary: Demonstrate practical collaboration with architecture, data, security, privacy, accessibility and service-management specialists.

outputs.title: Controlled release and evaluation
outputs.summary: Release proportionately, measure use and outcomes, and feed evidence back into prioritisation.

outputs.title: Harden-or-close decisions
outputs.summary: Apply explicit criteria for supporting successful capabilities or concluding unsuccessful experiments without unmanaged legacy.

outputs.title: Practice and role improvements
outputs.summary: Use delivery evidence to improve the operating model, team shape, workflow and specialist interfaces.

newInvestment.item: Year 2 peak digital product development team
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Retains the first-year pod and adds one full-stack or integration engineer and 0.5 FTE quality engineering and test automation to support concurrent product delivery and live-service resilience.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The team may lack the resilience to operate live services while supporting the wider Hub roadmap.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the Year 2 staffing profile against the confirmed product pipeline, live-service obligations and evidence from the first delivery cycles.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT product capability leadership with King’s Edge Portfolio Board
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team shape may not match the confirmed balance of product delivery and live-service work.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make the team’s operating practices routine. Establish reliable pipeline and capacity planning, a predictable discovery and release rhythm, regular quality and assurance activity, effective collaboration on incidents and maintenance, clear ownership and handover arrangements, and evidence-led review of product performance and benefits.

outputs.title: Routine pipeline and capacity cadence
outputs.summary: Maintain a transparent backlog and regular prioritisation and capacity decisions across product demands.

outputs.title: Predictable discovery and release rhythm
outputs.summary: Establish a repeatable cadence that balances discovery, delivery, quality, release and evaluation.

outputs.title: Live-service feedback loop
outputs.summary: Connect incidents, support evidence, maintenance and service performance directly into product prioritisation.

outputs.title: Ownership and handover model
outputs.summary: Clarify when the team retains responsibility, collaborates with service owners or transfers an enduring capability.

outputs.title: Product evidence and benefits review
outputs.summary: Use product analytics, research and operational evidence to assess value and decide what happens next.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices across the wider app roadmap
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, apply the established operating model across a growing portfolio of student journeys. Increase throughput and support concurrent work while preserving continuous user involvement, disciplined prioritisation, quality, embedded assurance, learning and sustainable ownership. Use evidence to refine the team shape, professional practices and balance between new delivery and live-service work.

outputs.title: Concurrent product delivery
outputs.summary: Support several product demands without fragmenting prioritisation, practices or accountability.

outputs.title: Consistent quality and assurance
outputs.summary: Apply common product, research, design, engineering, quality and assurance expectations across the roadmap.

outputs.title: Professional capability development
outputs.summary: Strengthen role development, mentoring, communities of practice and access to specialist leadership.

outputs.title: Balanced delivery and live-service capacity
outputs.summary: Plan explicitly for new development, maintenance, support, technical improvement and research.

outputs.title: Evidence-led team design
outputs.summary: Refine roles and capacity using throughput, quality, service and demand evidence rather than assumption.

newInvestment.item: Year 3 peak digital product development team
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before the 2028/29 staffing plan is fixed
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Continues the peak team through the final intensive year of wider-app delivery, concurrent live-service work and transition into an enduring capability.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Capacity may taper before the team has supported the principal wider-app transition and embedded sustainable practices.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the final mobilisation-year staffing profile against the confirmed roadmap, concurrent product demand and live-service responsibilities.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT product capability leadership
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team profile may not match the work required to deliver and operate the wider app.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: From November 2028 to June 2029, establish the multidisciplinary team, its recurrent staffing, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with product owners and specialist Digital and IT services as an enduring institutional capability. Ensure the team can respond to new priorities and continuously improve live products without reverting to disconnected local builds, separate procurements or unsupported prototypes.

outputs.title: Recurrent team and funding model
outputs.summary: Confirm the sustainable core staffing and funding route beyond mobilisation.

outputs.title: Enduring governance and decision rights
outputs.summary: Confirm authority over the pipeline, capacity, methods and escalation routes.

outputs.title: Professional leadership and career routes
outputs.summary: Embed role development, professional standards, mentoring and progression for the multidisciplinary team.

outputs.title: Stable specialist and service interfaces
outputs.summary: Confirm how the team works with architecture, data, integration, assurance, service management and product owners.

outputs.title: Continuous-improvement operating model
outputs.summary: Maintain regular discovery, delivery, evaluation and practice improvement after mobilisation ends.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £263,000 annual recurrent cost in constant 2026 prices.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before recurrent budgets and organisational structures are fixed for 2029/30
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Recurrent Digital and IT baseline, TBC
newInvestment.rationale: Retains two full-stack engineers, approximately 0.75 FTE product and experience design and approximately 0.75 FTE agile delivery and product operations.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The institution will lose the multidisciplinary development capability created through mobilisation.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the 3.5 FTE recurrent team model before the final mobilisation year ends.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with institutional investment governance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The team may reach the end of mobilisation without a funded route into business as usual.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm enduring product-capability leadership, prioritisation governance and the relationship to the Hub product and platform ownership under 4.1.2.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the accountable Student Experience Hub sponsor
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before transition to business as usual
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The permanent team may lack clear authority over its pipeline, practices and capacity.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm professional-development and specialist-practice support for the recurrent team.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before transition to business as usual
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The capability may persist as staffing capacity without the professional depth needed to remain effective.
